chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad from Al-Hasan from Jameel from Bukayr said,
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who sends his zakat, but it gets stolen or wasted. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is nothing upon him (no liability)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the zakat obligation if the money is stolen after being sent?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Zakat is discharged upon dispatch (*ibtida' al-irsal*), meaning the sender bears no liability if the funds are lost or stolen in transit. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *bara'ah al-asliyyah* (presumption of innocence/exemption) regarding the transfer of wealth, distinguishing it from cases where the recipient bears the risk. It underscores the ease (*taysir*) Islam places on believers in fulfilling financial obligations, provided the act of sending was executed with due diligence.
